purpose: Formalize and freeze, BEFORE any rerun, three distinct concepts the Phase 3F.1.5 second-pass protocol never separated for its reviewer, and which the forensic pass in 01-original-disagreement-forensics.json shows account for the majority of the failed detailed-agreement gate: (A) Discovery/Surfacing, (B) Semantic Representation, (C) Verified Semantic Representation. These must never be collapsed into one another when computing credit.

coreDistinction.A_DiscoverySurfacing: A candidate exists in the pipeline's inventory that MENTIONS or is textually located near content relevant to a claim. It has NOT been compiled into a structured representation and carries no assertion that it correctly or completely captures the claim. Its accountingRole in V2 is INVENTORY_ONLY or, when it independently flags a gap, SAFETY_FLAG.
coreDistinction.B_SemanticRepresentation: A candidate has been compiled into a structured representation (an IR rule, IR definition, or semantic coverage unit) whose asserted content semantically corresponds to the claim on the dimensions V2 checks (subject/action, posture, object, scope, economics, conditions, provenance, breadth). Its accountingRole is SUBSTANTIVE_REPRESENTATION. Representation does not by itself mean the representation has been independently checked for correctness.
coreDistinction.C_VerifiedSemanticRepresentation: A semantic representation (B) that has additionally passed the system's own independent verification layer (Phase 2E/3C verification, or an explicit second-pass/AI-judge confirmation) with no unresolved verifier finding contradicting it.
coreDistinction.whyThisMatters: Correct DISCOVERY of a claim's location is necessary for eventual representation but is not itself evidence the system understood or captured the claim's meaning. A pipeline can correctly find every relevant clause (perfect discovery) while compiling none of them faithfully (zero true representation) - discovery recall and representation recall are different numbers and must be reported separately (see 11-separated-product-metrics.json).

stateTaxonomy.definition: No candidate of any kind exists anywhere near the claim's source location. The claim is invisible to the entire downstream pipeline.

A DISCOVERY_CANDIDATE (INVENTORY_ONLY) textually overlaps the claim's source location but was never compiled into a structured representation, and no candidate at this location carries a SAFETY_FLAG surfacing it for review.
stateTaxonomy.note: This is the state most often mistaken for representation by a reviewer not told about the discovery/representation distinction - see 01-original-disagreement-forensics.json's DISCOVERY_VS_REPRESENTATION_CONFUSION cluster.

stateTaxonomy.definition: A candidate at the claim's location carries an explicit SAFETY_FLAG (a coverage-gap, verifier finding, or self-declared ambiguity) that surfaces the location for human review, without asserting any specific answer.
stateTaxonomy.note: This state can PREVENT a dangerous-omission classification (see 03-dangerous-omission-semantics.json) even though it earns no representation credit - honest surfacing is a distinct, valued outcome from correct representation.

stateTaxonomy.definition: A compiled representation (accountingRole SUBSTANTIVE_REPRESENTATION) semantically corresponds to the claim on all core dimensions, but has not been confirmed by an independent verification pass.
A compiled representation corresponds, and verification was attempted but could not reach a conclusion (e.g. the verifier itself returned INDETERMINATE).

A compiled representation corresponds on all core dimensions AND has been independently verified with no contradicting finding. This is V2's REPRESENTED / EXACT_SINGLE / EXACT_COMPOSITE disposition family.

A compiled representation corresponds on the CORE dimensions (subject/action/posture/object) but is silent on, or conflicts on, at least one non-core dimension (e.g. economics, a specific condition, breadth) the claim depends on. Credit is given proportionally; the missing dimension(s) must be named.
stateTaxonomy.countsTowardSemanticRepresentationRecall: PARTIAL - see 11-separated-product-metrics.json for how PARTIAL is weighted; never rounded up to full VERIFIED_SEMANTIC_REPRESENTATION credit
stateTaxonomy.relevantToDangerousOmission: Only if the missing dimension is itself CRITICAL/MATERIAL to the claim's operative effect (see 03-dangerous-omission-semantics.json's carve-out-without-the-rule-it-carves-out-of pattern).

stateTaxonomy.definition: No candidate corresponds to the claim on any core dimension, and no candidate at the claim's location surfaces the gap for review. This is a silent, uncaught coverage gap.
stateTaxonomy.note: This is V2's UNREPRESENTED disposition WITHOUT an accompanying safety flag - the most dangerous state in the taxonomy.

stateTaxonomy.definition: A candidate corresponds to the claim's location/topic well enough to be considered relevant, but the candidate ITSELF explicitly declares its own answer unresolved/uncertain (e.g. it names ambiguous or unavailable evidence) rather than asserting a confident position.
stateTaxonomy.note: This state is safe (surfaced, not silent) even though it earns no representation credit. Phase 3F.1.5's second-pass reviewer had no equivalent bucket and collapsed this into UNREPRESENTED - the single largest source of the failed 37.3% detailed-agreement score (21 of 32 disagreements, all binary-credit AGREEMENTS). Any future reviewer protocol MUST give this state its own label, separate from both HONESTLY_UNSUPPORTED and UNREPRESENTED.

stateTaxonomy.definition: A compiled representation exists and corresponds on subject/location, but asserts a materially different, conflicting answer (wrong direction, wrong basis, wrong scope) than the ground truth claim.
stateTaxonomy.note: Arguably MORE dangerous than a silent omission, since it actively misinforms rather than merely being absent - flagged separately in the dangerous-omission accounting, not conflated with it.

stateTaxonomy.definition: Two or more mutually irreconcilable candidate interpretations correspond to the claim about equally well, and forcing a single winner would manufacture false precision the evidence does not support.
stateTaxonomy.note: Safe (surfaced) but uncredited. The near-tie-score threshold for declaring AMBIGUOUS vs. picking a winner is a genuine open methodological question (see doc-a::II::2.21-returned-payments in 01-original-disagreement-forensics.json) not resolved by this taxonomy alone.

stateTaxonomy.definition: The ground-truth unit itself cannot be resolved to a specific source excerpt (UNRESOLVED_DESCRIPTION_ONLY) or is independently flagged GT_REQUIRES_DOMAIN_REVIEW, making a confident disposition on either side unreliable regardless of candidate quality.
stateTaxonomy.note: Excluded from clean aggregate recall/omission denominators, exactly as Phase 3F.1.5 already handled GT_REQUIRES_DOMAIN_REVIEW units - never silently dropped, always reported as a distinct excluded count.

creditCollapseRules.principle: Correct discovery alone must NEVER be promoted to VERIFIED_SEMANTIC_REPRESENTATION credit, and a compiled-but-unverified representation must never be silently promoted to VERIFIED credit either. Each of the three recall metrics in 11-separated-product-metrics.json is computed from an explicit, disjoint subset of the states above - never from a collapsed union.

note: This taxonomy is frozen as of this artifact's generation. Per Section 7's environment-block finding (04-live-semantic-judge-run.json), no rerun using this taxonomy occurs in Phase 3F.1.5.1 - it is preserved here for the future iteration that will execute once a model credential is available.
